text:
marta: Heads up — spotted an adapter coercion weirdness in prod this morning. Thought it was transient but saw it across a few requests.

marta: Example tool payload we got back (sanitized):
```
{"tool_response": "null", "meta": {"declared_type": "string"}}
```

marta: Our structured validator then turned that into actual JSON null for the field and downstream code assumed absence -> NPE in reranker.

jamal: Ah — so adapter is doing a value coercion step before validation? Is this the new permissive parsing fallback we added last quarter?

priya: We added a permissive parse for older model variants, but it should only coerce when schema type is null/nullable. This looks like it coerced a string-literal "null" into null unconditionally.

alex: Confirming. I just traced a sample request: adapter.parse() has a call to `coerce_literals()` that does `if val in ["null","true","false"] then json.loads(val)` — blunt but convenient; didn't guard on schema type.

sara: That explains it. For strict rollout we reject on mismatch, for permissive we coerce. But does the rollout toggle flip coercion too? We intended it to control only rejection behavior.

marta: Right now the canary that turned strict validation on also changed parsing mode inadvertently — missed in the feature flag.

jamal: Action: revert parsing change in the canary and add an explicit gate: `ALLOW_COERCION` tied to adapter config. Also we should add telemetry to count coercions and sampled request IDs.

priya: +1. We need a dashboard tile showing `adapter.coercion.count` and `validator.reject.count` side-by-side with sample traces. Ops hit this because the reject rate was low but coerced requests caused downstream errors.

alex: Proposed quick fix:
- PR to adapter: only coerce literals if schema declares type in (null, boolean, number)
- Add metric `adapter.coercion.type=<literal>` and `adapter.coercion.allowed_by_flag=true/false`
- Add slow-sampling of 1% logs to `coercion_sample_id` for full payload capture

sara: For rollout UX: the Console should expose a boolean for "enable parsing coercion" separate from "strict schema enforcement". Right now flags are overloaded.

marta: Agreed. UX ticket: create a small toggle under model route settings + note about compatibility with old model variants.

jamal: Also, routing/quotas: if strict validation rejects, we currently return 400 which counts against customer quota and surfaces as errors. Maybe fallback-route to permissive model variant instead of consuming quota? Thoughts?

priya: We discussed automatic fallback earlier. For abrupt rejections we should route to the legacy permissive variant for a short window and mark the response with `x-fallback-reason=validation_reject` — and metric `route.fallback.validation_reject`.

alex: Implementation detail: route fallback should be best-effort and not synchronous if customer opted-out. We'll need Console opt-in and a per-customer policy.

marta: I'll open three PRs: adapter guard + metrics, Console toggle, and routing policy fallback skeleton. Assigning reviewers: @jamal @priya for adapter, @sara for Console UX, @alex for routing.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline queued for branch marta/adapter-coercion-fix (build #4821). Logs: https://ci.internal/4821 :eyes:

ci-bot: Canary deploy to staging scheduled in 15m. Will post outcome.

jamal: Thanks — once canary verifies we should flip the strict canary off until the Console toggle lands.

sara: I'll add a temporary dashboard alert rule: if `adapter.coercion.count > 5` in 5m AND `validator.reject.count < 2` then page team on #eng-oncall (we want to catch silent coercions).

marta: Great. Assigning follow-ups in the PRs. If anyone sees additional weird literal cases ("None", "<nil>") add them to the PR comments so we can extend whitelist heuristics instead of ad-hoc rules. :+1:
